title: A Study to Assess the Safety of Marstacimab and How Well it Works in People With Mild to Moderate Hemophilia A or B Without Inhibitors
official: AN OPEN-LABEL STUDY TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF MARSTACIMAB PROPHYLAXIS IN ADOLESCENT AND ADULT PARTICIPANTS WITH MILD (FVIII OR FIX ACTIVITY >5% TO ≤15%) TO MODERATE (≥1% TO ≤5%) HEMOPHILIA A OR B WITHOUT INHIBITORS
summary:
This is an open-label, multicenter study evaluating the efficacy and safety of marstacimab prophylaxis in approximately 95 male and female adolescents and adults aged 12 to \<75 years with mild to moderate hemophilia A or B without inhibitors who have a severe bleeding phenotype. Eligible participants must have baseline factor VIII or factor IX activity levels \>1% to ≤15% and a history of clinically significant bleeding despite prior treatment with either on-demand factor replacement therapy or routine factor prophylaxis.

The study will compare bleeding outcomes and other efficacy measures during a historical 12-month period of prescribed factor replacement therapy prior to study entry with outcomes observed during a 12-month treatment phase in which participants receive marstacimab 150 mg administered subcutaneously once weekly. Participants will be enrolled into 2 cohorts based on their treatment regimen before study entry: a prior on-demand treatment cohort and a prior routine prophylaxis treatment cohort.

Female participants with severe hemophilia A or B without inhibitors may also be enrolled on a case-by-case basis. Data from these participants will contribute to safety assessments, and separate descriptive analyses of efficacy outcomes will be performed for all female participants.

The study will also evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of marstacimab during a long-term extension (LTE) treatment phase of up to 36 months. Participants who complete the 12-month treatment phase may continue into the LTE phase.

Participants may be in the study for approximately 50 months, including a 12-month treatment phase and a long-term extension phase of up to 36 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Male or female, 12 to less than 75 years of age and weighing at least 35 kg.
* Moderate hemophilia A or B (factor VIII or factor IX activity ≥1% to ≤5%), or Mild hemophilia A or B (factor VIII or factor IX activity \>5% to ≤15%).
* Females with severe hemophilia A or B may be eligible on a case-by-case basis following discussion with sponsor.
* No history of factor VIII or factor IX inhibitors within the 5 years before screening.
* At least 12 months of medical records and/or bleeding diary data documenting hemophilia-related bleeding episodes and factor VIII or factor IX replacement therapy prior to screening.
* Participants receiving on-demand factor replacement therapy must have had at least 2 treated bleeding episodes during the 12 months before screening (surgical or procedural bleeds do not count).
* Participants receiving routine prophylactic factor replacement therapy must have received a stable prophylaxis regimen for at least 12 months with ≥80% compliance and at least 1 treated bleeding episode in the 12 months before screening (excluding surgical or procedural bleeds).

Exclusion Criteria

* Current evidence of a congenital or acquired thrombophilic disorder, including antithrombin III deficiency, Factor V Leiden mutation, prothrombin G20210A mutation, protein C deficiency, protein S deficiency, or antiphospholipid syndrome.
* Known coronary artery disease, history of venous or arterial thrombosis, or other clinically significant ischemic disease.
* Any bleeding disorder other than hemophilia A or hemophilia B.
* Any medical, psychiatric, or laboratory abnormality that, in the investigator's opinion, could increase risk or interfere with study participation.
* Current use of bypassing agents, non-factor replacement therapies for hemophilia, or prior hemophilia gene therapy.
* Regular treatment with immunomodulatory medications.
* Use of prohibited medications, including systemic antifibrinolytic agents, medications that increase bleeding risk, or certain nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), as specified by the protocol.
* Use of estrogen-containing hormonal therapies (including contraceptives and HRTs) within 30 days before or during the study, or depot medroxyprogesterone acetate within 6 months before or during the study.
* Receipt of another investigational drug or vaccine within 30 days or 5 half-lives before study treatment (whichever is longer), or planned participation in another investigational study during this study.
* Significant renal or hepatic impairment or clinically significant laboratory abnormalities at screening.
* Platelet count \<100,000/μL, hemoglobin \<10 g/dL (with limited exceptions), fibrinogen below the lower limit of normal, or prolonged prothrombin time.
* CD4 count ≤200 cells/μL in participants with HIV infection.
* Clinically significant electrocardiogram abnormalities at screening.
* Planned surgical procedure during the study period.
* Known hypersensitivity to hamster protein or any component of the study treatment.
* Study site personnel, sponsor personnel directly involved in the conduct of the study, or their immediate family members.
